# Volume 3 — Chapter XXVII Mutual Confidences

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

That winter, March arrived in the manner of an exceptionally gentle and docile lamb, producing days filled with crisp, golden, and tingling air, with every one giving way to a frosty pink dusk that slowly melted into a magical realm of moonlight.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0000 }

The loom of April examinations cast a shadow across the young women at Tabby’s Place. Hard study occupied them; even Cressy had devoted herself to notebooks and text with a tenacity that one would not have anticipated from her.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0001 }

“I’m going to take the Johnson Scholarship in Mathematics,” she declared serenely. “I could win the one in Greek without difficulty, but I prefer to win the mathematical one since I wish to demonstrate to Ezra that I am truly remarkably brilliant.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0002 }

“Ezra prefers you for those large brown eyes and that lopsided smile of yours rather than for any of the intelligence held beneath your curls,” Nell remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0003 }

“During my youth, women were not expected to understand Mathematics,” Aunt Euphemia remarked. “However, the era has shifted. I am unsure if these changes are entirely positive. Do you possess cooking skills, Cressy?”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0004 }

“No, I have not prepared any food ever in my life, save for a gingerbread that turned out poorly—sunken in the center and raised at the margins. You are familiar with that sort. However, Aunty, once I commence learning to cook in serious truth, do you not suppose that the same intellect allowing me to secure a mathematical scholarship will likewise permit me to master cooking equally well?”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0005 }

“Perhaps,” Aunt Euphemia remarked with care. “I am not criticizing advanced schooling for women. An M.A. is held by my daughter. Cooking is also within her skill. However, instruction in cooking was given to her by me prior to allowing her to be taught Mathematics by a university professor.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0006 }

A letter arrived from Miss Tabby Linden in the middle of March, announcing that she and Miss Maria had chosen to stay overseas for one more year.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0007 }

“Therefore Tabby’s Place might be yours for the following winter as well,” was her written message. “Maria and my intention is to make a quick trip to Egypt. My wish is to view the Sphinx a single time prior to my death.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0008 }

“Imagine those two women ‘travelling around Egypt’! I wonder whether they will gaze up at the Sphinx while knitting,” Honora chuckled.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0009 }

“I am extremely happy that Tabby’s Place remains ours for one more year,” Mabel remarked. “My fear was that they would return, which would shatter our delightful small haven here, casting us unfortunate, inexperienced young ones back into the harsh realm of boardinghouses.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0010 }

“I’m going for a walk in the park,” declared Cressy, throwing her book to one side. “It seems to me that upon reaching eighty, I will be pleased that I took a stroll in the park this evening.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0011 }

“In what way?” inquired Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0012 }

“Accompany me and I will explain, honey.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0013 }

In their strolling, they took in every bit of the magic and mystery belonging to a March evening. It possessed a great stillness and mildness, enveloped by a vast, white, contemplative quietude—a quietude that nevertheless had numerous tiny, silvery noises woven through it, which could be detected if one listened using their soul as much as their ears. Down an elongated pine-forested passage, the girls roamed toward what appeared to be the very center of an abundant, deep-red winter sunset.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0014 }

“If I merely possessed the skill, I’d return home and compose a poem this very instant,” Cressy announced, stopping in a clearing as the green ends of the pine trees were being dyed by a pink glow. “Everything is so marvellous in this place—this vast, pale silence, along with those deep-colored trees that appear to be constantly contemplating.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0015 }

“‘The first temples of God were the woods,’” Nell softly quoted. “In a place like this, a person cannot avoid feeling adoring and reverent. Walking among the pines always makes me feel so close to Him.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0016 }

“I am the most joyful girl on earth, Nell,” abruptly admitted Cressy.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0017 }

“So Mr. Hale has finally requested your hand in marriage?” asked Nell composedly.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0018 }

“Indeed. Furthermore, my sneezing occurred thrice during his proposal. Was that not dreadful? Nevertheless, my answer of ‘yes’ came practically prior to his conclusion—such was my fear that his decision might alter and he would cease. My happiness is absolute infatuation. Previously, it seemed truly unbelievable to me that Ezra could ever harbor affection for someone as lighthearted as myself.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0019 }

“Cressy, you’re not really frivolous,” Nell said solemnly. “Deep down below that frivolous surface of yours, you possess a sweet, faithful, womanly little soul. Why do you conceal it to such a degree?”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0020 }

“Queen Nell, it is impossible for me to act otherwise. Your assessment is correct—my core is not frivolous. Nevertheless, my soul is covered by a kind of frivolous outer layer that I am unable to shed. To quote Mrs. Poyser, changing it would require me to be hatched a second time and hatched in a different way. Ezra, however, understands my true self and affectionally accepts me, including my frivolous nature. My feelings for him are mutual. Discovering my love for him astonished me more than anything else ever has. Loving an unattractive man was something I had previously deemed impossible. Imagine my situation dwindling to a single suitor. Furthermore, a suitor by the name of Ezra! My intention, though, is to address him as Ez. Such a name is delightfully short and sharp. A nickname for Orlando would have been impossible.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0021 }

“How do Hector and Orlando figure into this?”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0022 }

“Oh, at Christmas I informed them that I could not possibly wed either one. Recalling that I once considered it a possibility appears so amusing at present. Because they were so deeply hurt, I wept over the two of them—wailed, in fact. However, I was certain that just a single man existed on earth whom I could ever take as a husband. For a change, I had reached my own decision, and doing so proved quite simple as well. Experiencing such certainty feels wonderful, especially realizing that this conviction belongs to you rather than another person.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0023 }

“Are you of the opinion that you can sustain this?”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0024 }

“Deciding, you are asking? I am uncertain, yet Ez supplied me with a magnificent guideline. He states, whenever I am confused, merely to act in the way I would desire to have acted when I am eighty years old. In any case, Ez is able to decide fast enough, and having an excess of mind within one home would be unpleasant.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0025 }

“In what manner will your mother and father respond?”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0026 }

“Father will not say very much. He believes all my actions are right. Mother, however, will speak. Oh, her tongue is going to be just as Byrney as her nose. Even so, everything will turn out all right in the end.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0027 }

“When you wed Mr. Hale, Cressy, there are quite a few things you have always possessed that you will need to surrender.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0028 }

“Yet he will be mine. Those other matters won't be missed by me. Our wedding is set for a year from the coming June. You are aware that Ez finishes his studies at St. Columbia this spring. Following that, a small mission church located down on Tanner Street in the slums will be taken over by him. Picture me living in the slums! Nevertheless, I would travel to that place or even to Greenland’s icy mountains alongside him.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0029 }

“And here we have the young woman who swore she would only wed a wealthy man,” Nell remarked, addressing a young pine tree.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0030 }

“Oh, do not bring up the foolish things I did when I was young. The way I have been wealthy is how cheerfully I will be poor. You will witness it. Learning to cook and altering dresses is what I intend to do. Ever since I have resided at Tabby’s Place, I have mastered marketing; and one entire summer, I gave lessons to a Sunday School class. According to Aunt Euphemia, marrying Ez will destroy his career. However, I will not. Although I am aware that I lack substantial sense or seriousness, I possess something far superior—the ability to get people to like me. A man who lisps and regularly gives testimony in prayer-meeting lives in Harborough. His words are, ‘If you can’t thine like an electric thtar thine like a candlethtick.’ Ez will have a small candlestick in me.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0031 }

“Cressy, you cannot be reformed. Ah, my affection for you is so deep that delivering pleasant, brief, celebratory remarks is impossible for me. However, your joy brings immense gladness to my heart.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0032 }

“I understand. That genuine affection fills your large gray eyes, Nell. Eventually, I will gaze at you with that same expression. Is it true that you will be marrying Cyril, Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0033 }

“My beloved Cressida, have you ever known about the renowned Betty Baxter, who ‘refused a man before he’d axed her’? I do not intend to copy that famous woman by either rejecting or taking anyone prior to his ‘axing’ me.”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0034 }

“Every person in Wexcombe is aware that Cyril is head over heels for you,” Cressy stated openly. “And he has your love, doesn’t he, Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0035 }

“I—I suppose so,” Nell admitted unwillingly. It seemed to her that she should have been turning red while admitting this; yet she was not; instead, she invariably flushed deeply whenever anyone mentioned Hugh Carrow or Rowena Calder when she was present. Hugh Carrow and Rowena Calder meant nothing to her—nothing whatsoever. Still, Nell had stopped attempting to examine why she turned red. Regarding Cyril, she was certainly infatuated with him—utterly infatuated. How could she avoid it? Did he not represent her ideal? Who could withstand such magnificent dark eyes, and that beseeching voice? Were not fifty percent of the Wexcombe girls intensely jealous? And what a delightful sonnet he had delivered to her, alongside a box of violets, for her birthday! Nell had committed every single word of it to memory. It was quite fine work for that sort of poetry, as well. Not quite on par with Keats or Shakespeare—even Nell’s infatuation was not so extreme that she believed that. Yet it was quite respectable magazine poetry. Furthermore, it was written for her—not for Laura or Beatrice or the Maid of Athens, but for her, Nell Harcourt. Having someone declare in poetic rhythm that her eyes were morning stars—that her cheek possessed the color taken from the dawn—that her lips were crimson beyond the roses of Paradise, was wonderfully romantic. Hugh would never have considered composing a sonnet to her eyebrows. On the other hand, Hugh possessed an appreciation for humor. She had on one occasion shared a amusing tale with Cyril—and he had failed to get the point. She remembered the friendly laugh she and Hugh had shared over that same story, and questioned with some discomfort whether existing alongside a man lacking humor might turn out to be rather dull eventually. Still, how could anyone anticipate that a somber, mysterious hero would appreciate the funny aspect of life? It would be entirely absurd.
{: #nw-v03-c27-p0036 }
